_readme: Stonkhouse address book. Every entry carries the call that proved it. `confirmed: true` means an eth_getCode or eth_call was actually run against a chain-4663 RPC and returned the stated result. Never add an address here without that check, and never copy one out of a frontend bundle without re-deriving it from chain state.
_reconfirmedBy: ops pass, cast 1.3.5 against https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com. Every `confirmed: true` row on chain 4663 below was re-read in this pass, not copied from recon. The 2026-09-13 redesign pass restructured the file (registry moved to history, `ours.clearinghouse` added, 46630 verdict corrected) without re-reading addresses.
_redesign_2026_09_13: The vault no longer reads an Overcall registry, lists on Overcall's order book, pays an Overcall fee item, or answers EIP-1271. It reads the option tuple from the clearinghouse it was constructed with (`vault.clear()`), numbers its own cycles, lists ONE PARTIAL_RESTRICTED Seaport order with itself as zone, and writes exactly the filled contracts inside Seaport's authorizeOrder hook. Everything under `_history_overcall` below is kept as recon evidence and is NOT wired into anything.
_sources: contracts/docs/DEPLOY.md (redesign rehearsal record, S4, fork block 62533535)
_notStale: Addresses in this file are immutable contract addresses and do not go stale. Cycle data (option ids, strikes, exerciseTimestamp, expiryTimestamp) DOES go stale weekly and is deliberately NOT in this file: the keeper creates each week's option type on the clearinghouse itself, and the vault's `optionId()`, `cycleStrikeUsdg()`, `cycleExerciseTs()`, `cycleExpiryTs()` are the live truth.

4663.name: Robinhood Chain
4663.type: Arbitrum Orbit L2, settles to Ethereum mainnet
4663._codeSizeLimit: Chain 4663 enforces a 98,304 B contract code limit, not EIP-170's 24,576 B (verified with eth_call --create probes: 98,304 B deploys, 98,305 B fails `max code size exceeded`; owner decision D17). The Vault runtime is above 24,576 B and is accepted here. `foundry.toml` sets code_size_limit = 98304; anvil rehearsals need `--code-size-limit 98304`; `forge script --broadcast` needs `--non-interactive`.

rpc._backupLimitation: The publicnode backup REJECTS eth_getLogs over old ranges with 'Archive requests require a personal token'. It is fine for eth_call / eth_getCode / eth_blockNumber and for recent-range logs. The indexer must use the primary.
rpc._userAgentGotcha: Both public RPCs return HTTP 403 to a client that sends no User-Agent (python urllib does this by default). Set one. curl and cast are fine.
rpc._nodeSkew: The primary load-balances across nodes measured ~4,000 blocks apart, and keeps only a few thousand trailing blocks of state. Start anvil forks and run them within minutes.

blockscout._cloudflare: Behind a Cloudflare managed challenge that keys on the ABSENCE of a Referer header. Any Referer value at all clears it. Browsers send one automatically, so links from the web app work; server-side clients (forge, curl, the indexer) get an HTML interstitial instead of JSON. For READING the API use ops/bsproxy.js or add a Referer. For SOURCE VERIFICATION do not use it at all: verify through Sourcify (`forge verify-contract --verifier sourcify --chain 4663`) and let Blockscout import the match ('Verify & publish → via Sourcify').
blockscout._rateLimit: Hosted Blockscout instance; throttles anonymous traffic with status=0 'Too many requests'.

sourcify._what: The source-verification path for the vault and both libraries. Holds exact matches for Valorem Clear and the TokenURIGenerator already. Never exercised for our contracts (fork only); the first mainnet deploy is the first run.

alternates._note: Display only. None is a Blockscout, none has a contract-verification API, none should be depended on programmatically.
alternates._preferredNonCloudflareLink: https://stonkscan.io — same /address|/tx|/token/{x} shape, no redirects, no Cloudflare gate.

valoremClear.what: ValoremOptionsClearinghouse ('Valorem Clear'), Overcall's unmodified upstream instance. valorem-core @6436c823, solc 0.8.16. Holds the collateral, mints the option ERC-1155 and the claim NFT, settles exercise. This is the DEFAULT clearinghouse the vault is constructed with (Deploy.s.sol `CLEARINGHOUSE`); the vault may instead target our own instance from script/DeployClear.s.sol (see `ours.clearinghouse`). The vault writes here only inside a Seaport fill (authorizeOrder → clear.write) and keeps its own claim NFT; the keeper creates each week's option type here with newOptionType (permissionless).
valoremClear.evidence: eth_getCode -> 16110 bytes (re-read 2026-09-12 block 61322378). Sourcify exact_match 2026-09-10T13:24:56Z. eth_call option(0x7dc3fe3e..) returned the NVDA/USDG option struct with underlyingAmount 1e18, exerciseAmount 246000000. feesEnabled() -> false, feeBps() -> 15, feeTo() -> 0xdAe7e82A....

liveState._feeSwitchWarning: setFeesEnabled(bool) is feeTo-only with NO timelock, and setFeeTo emits NO event (the nomination is visible only in storage slot 3). The 15 bps is charged on NOTIONAL, not premium, and write() pulls underlyingAmount*n + fee in one transferFrom, on every fill. If it flips on, Vault.rollOpen and every fill revert ValoremFeeNotAccepted until the admin calls acceptValoremFee(true); the fill floor then values the fee at spot. That is deliberate.

seaport16.what: Seaport 1.6, canonical deployment. The vault is the OFFERER and the ZONE of its one PARTIAL_RESTRICTED listing per cycle: it pre-validates the order hash on chain via seaport.validate() (so an empty signature fills; there is no EIP-1271), and Seaport calls the vault's authorizeOrder before any transfer and validateOrder after, on every fulfil path. Nobody but Seaport may call the hooks (NotSeaport).
seaport16.evidence: eth_getCode -> 23981 bytes. information() -> ('1.6', domainSeparator 0xa6b20d2b6f71c703cd333de0c921d303988fb481ff2982df74a21e19af3730b0, conduitController 0x00000000F9490004C11Cef243f5400493c00Ad63). Re-read 2026-09-12. TSTORE/TLOAD and MCOPY verified on 4663; the live Seaport's TLOAD self-test passed at deployment (integrations/seaport.md §2). Verify.s.sol pins this runtime's extcodehash.
seaport16.runtimeExtcodehash: 0x95809b70…4a00 (pinned in contracts/script/Verify.s.sol; read the full value from the script)

seaportConduitController.what: Seaport ConduitController. Present on this chain and unused by us: the vault's listings carry conduitKey 0x00..00 and Seaport pulls the freshly minted ERC-1155 directly. Deploy.s.sol's preflight requires Seaport to report this canonical controller.
seaportConduitController.evidence: eth_getCode -> 8820 bytes; matches the controller Seaport's own information() reports.
seaportConduitController._trap: getConduit(bytes32(0)) on 4663 returns conduit 0xf9ed144bacaed98d0f3899b8b56c965d1a966d08 with exists=true, and there IS real conduit runtime code at that address. Seaport does NOT use it — it special-cases conduitKey == 0 and transfers directly. Any code shaped `if (conduitKey != 0) approve(getConduit(conduitKey))` must keep the `!= 0` guard. AdapterSeaport's constructor does. The non-zero conduitKey constructor branch is untested in production shape.

usdg.what: USDG, the exercise asset and the premium currency. 6 decimals. Paxos-issued, behind a proxy. Instant pause, per-address freeze (enforced on the transferFrom SPENDER too, so a frozen Seaport blocks every fill), wipe and burn-from powers; 27 freezes observed on 4663, none lifted. A pause or a freeze of the vault or the Clear STRANDS the week's close (the vault keeps the claim, anyone can retryStrandedClaim) and defers the USDG leg of a redemption (UsdgLegDeferred).

nvdaStockToken.what: NVDA Stock Token — the vault's underlying asset and Valorem's underlyingAsset. 18 decimals, beacon proxy. A debt security issued by Robinhood Assets (Jersey) Limited, not equity. The issuer can pause transfers, blocklist an address (a blocklisted vault strands the close even in an unassigned week), adminBurn supply with no pause/blocklist guard (the vault's NAV is then the honest max(balance + locked − reserved, 0) and settled queue entries take a pro-rata ReserveHaircut), and change the multiplier (which can DECREASE).
nvdaStockToken.evidence: eth_getCode -> 283 bytes (beacon proxy). symbol() -> 'NVDA'. decimals() -> 18. oraclePaused() -> false. uiMultiplier() -> 1000775159164630595. Re-read 2026-09-12.
nvdaStockToken._uiMultiplier: ERC-8056 display multiplier. DISPLAY ONLY. The vault's internal maths use raw balances, and the Chainlink answer ALREADY has the multiplier applied — never apply it twice. Do not arm on a day the multiplier is scheduled to change.
nvdaStockToken._oraclePaused: An issuer broadcast flag on the token. Vault._requireOracleLive() staticcalls it and reverts OraclePaused when true, at arm AND at every fill, so the vault holds spot and sells nothing. It does not itself stop Chainlink transmitting.

multicall3.what: Multicall3, canonical address. Used by the keeper and the web app to batch reads.

clearFeeTo.what: ValoremClear.feeTo() on Overcall's instance: the key that can flip the 15 bps engine fee switch (no timelock, no event on nomination). An unfunded EOA, not a contract, not a Safe. It is ALSO Overcall's off-chain premium fee recipient, which no longer concerns us: the redesigned vault's listings carry no fee item and this address appears nowhere in the vault. Monitor it (ETH/nonce activity, FeeSwitchUpdated, Clear storage slot 3) when the vault targets Overcall's Clear; irrelevant when the vault targets our own.
clearFeeTo.evidence: eth_getCode -> 0 bytes. ValoremClear.feeTo() returns this address. Previously recorded in this file as `overcallFeeRecipient` (consideration[1].recipient on Overcall's orders); renamed 2026-09-13 because the fee item is gone.

nvdaUsdFeed.what: Chainlink AggregatorProxy, 'RHNVDA / USD', phaseId 1, 8 decimals. The vault's spot source for the OTM band gate (both bounds at arm, the floor at every fill), the premium floor at every fill, and the UI. NEVER consulted in the settlement path.
nvdaUsdFeed.evidence: eth_getCode -> 9571 bytes. description() -> 'RHNVDA / USD'. decimals() -> 8. latestRoundData() -> (roundId 18446744073709552641, answer 21829793457 = $218.2979, startedAt 1789157011, updatedAt 1789157023 = Fri 2026-09-11 20:03:43 UTC). Re-read 2026-09-12 at block 61322378, age 22.5 h.
nvdaUsdFeed._STALENESS_WARNING: The 86400 s heartbeat is NOT honoured while the US equity market is shut. Observed gaps: 21 h worst intra-week, 52 h 04 m over a normal weekend, 78 h 14 m over the Labor Day weekend. Rounds restart at 00:00:54 UTC Monday (20:00 ET Sunday). A 24-hour staleness rule would block rollOpen every Saturday and Sunday and guarantee a 0% week. Vault.maxPriceAge ships at 4 days for exactly this reason (script/Deploy.s.sol MAX_PRICE_AGE), bounded in bytecode to [1 hour, 7 days]. The frozen weekend value can predate the close by hours (3 of 12 closures froze 2.2–4.6 h early), so arm during the regular session.
nvdaUsdFeed._bindToTheProxy: Bind to this proxy, never to aggregator(). The proxy exists to have its aggregator rotated; proposedAggregator() is currently zero.

nvdaUsdFeedSecondary.what: Second Chainlink AggregatorProxy for RHNVDA/USD (SVR twin). Byte-identical to the primary proxy and wraps the same DualAggregator; returns the same answer and updatedAt. Held as a documented fallback only — the vault is wired to the primary.
nvdaUsdFeedSecondary.evidence: Listed as `secondaryProxyAddress` in Chainlink's feeds-robinhood-mainnet.json; bytecode sha256 identical to the primary; same answer/updatedAt at the same block (ops/recon/R5-price-feed.md section 2.1).

usdgUsdFeed.what: Chainlink AggregatorProxy 'USDG / USD', 8 decimals. Optional, display only. Nothing in the contracts reads it.

sequencerUptimeFeed.what: Chainlink L2 sequencer uptime feed. DOES NOT EXIST on chain 4663.
sequencerUptimeFeed.evidence: Chainlink's feeds-robinhood-mainnet.json has 57 feeds and ZERO sequencer/uptime entries.
sequencerUptimeFeed._consequence: The standard Arbitrum-style sequencer-down guard cannot be implemented here. A sequencer stall surfaces as a stale price, but at maxPriceAge = 4 days the vault's StalePrice check does NOT catch it for days: watch L2 head liveness directly (ops/alerts.md §26).

tokenUriGenerator.what: Valorem's TokenURIGenerator. Renders the option/claim ERC-1155 metadata. Informational; nothing in Stonkhouse calls it.

create2Factory.what: The deterministic CREATE2 factory forge uses for library deploys. SeaportOrderLib and ValoremLib are deployed through it, so their addresses depend only on their bytecode (see `ours`).
create2Factory.evidence: Used by the S4 rehearsal on a fork of 4663 (contracts/docs/DEPLOY.md); present on the live chain per forge's deploy path.

weth.what: WETH on 4663. Not used by Stonkhouse. Recorded so nobody has to go looking.

seaportListingShape._what: The exact Seaport 1.6 order the redesigned vault authorises, enforced on chain by contracts/src/lib/SeaportOrderLib.sol (approveListing) and consumed by Seaport's hooks (authorizeOrder / validateOrder on the vault). Do not invent a variant: approveListing reverts on every deviation (BadOrderType, BadZone, BadZoneHash, BadConduitKey, BadConsiderationLength, BadVaultRecipient, PremiumNotDivisibleByOrderSize, UnitPriceExceedsStrike, ListingOutlivesExercise, ListingStartsInFuture, BadCounter, OfferExceedsCapacity, ...).
seaportListingShape.endTimeSource: ≤ vault.cycleExerciseTs() (the option's exercise timestamp; the hook refuses fills after it regardless, WriteWindowClosed)
seaportListingShape.counterSource: seaport.getCounter(vault), read live immediately before authorising

consideration.amount: unitPrice6 * N, gross % N == 0, unitPrice6 ≤ strike

seaportListingShape.signature: empty (0x). The vault pre-validates the hash on Seaport (seaport.validate in approveListing); there is no key and no EIP-1271 hook.
seaportListingShape._fill: Any Seaport 1.6 fulfil function. Seaport calls vault.authorizeOrder BEFORE any transfer on every path; the hook re-checks the live listing, Listed, not halted, the clock, the fee switch, the oracle, the band FLOOR and the premium floor at live spot (PremiumBelowFloorAtFill), sizes written + k, writes exactly k on the clearinghouse and approves the minted tokens; Seaport moves them to the buyer and the USDG to the vault; vault.validateOrder then reverts InventoryLeftBehind unless the vault's option balance is back at the pre-fill baseline. Gas: first fill ≈ 470k, top-up ≈ 245k (spike figures); the fill page pre-flights with ~500k.
seaportListingShape._venue: The self-hosted fill page (/vault/nvda/cycle, fed by the keeper's /orders through the web server). There is no other venue and no off-chain book.

_history_overcall._status: HISTORY, NOT WIRED. Everything in this block was live recon evidence for the pre-redesign design, in which the vault read Overcall's per-market registry for the weekly strike ladder, listed on Overcall's order book with a 5% fee item, and answered EIP-1271 for its order hash. Since 2026-09-13 none of it is referenced by the contracts, the keeper, the indexer or the web app. It is kept because ops/recon/ cites it and because the same Overcall key still holds the fee switch on the default clearinghouse (see contracts.clearFeeTo).

_TRAP_JUGGERNAUT_REGISTRY.what: Overcall's frontend config object for chain 4663 has BOTH a `registries` map (one registry per market) AND a top-level `registry` key. The top-level key is 0x65dD407955912Be814f723724cE60f91ebd72616, the JUGGERNAUT memecoin market, NOT NVDA. Both are the same 5,905-byte OvercallRegistry bytecode and both answer every getter; only the immutable `collateralToken` differs.
_TRAP_JUGGERNAUT_REGISTRY._nowMoot: The vault has no registry parameter and no RegistryAssetMismatch check any more; there is nothing to mis-wire. Recorded so nobody re-derives the trap while reading the old recon.

registries._what: One OvercallRegistry per market, one per collateral token. All 11 were the same 5,905-byte contract; they differ only in the immutable collateralToken. All used USDG as exerciseToken and the same Valorem Clear.
registries._deployer: All 11 were deployed and owned by 0x408adcFFebDF48EC23F1E3811A91AeD3cC951CC0, the sender of all newOptionType calls on this chain before Stonkhouse. A single EOA.

NVDA.evidence: eth_getCode -> 5905 bytes; collateralToken()/exerciseToken()/clearinghouse()/cycleNumber() -> 1/isWritingOpen() -> true read live 2026-09-12. Fully verified source on Blockscout and Sourcify exact_match.

GME._note: cycleNumber() was 0: proof that 'no cycle yet' was a reachable registry state

overcallOrderShape._what: The order shape Overcall's own book required, copied from the one real filled NVDA order (orderHash 0xa11edb6292fa1789a13419830d5bd1b5a0145954d3e8352bb6ff776ca67de522): PARTIAL_OPEN (1), zone 0x0, two USDG consideration items (95% writer, 5% to 0xdAe7e82A…, floored per contract), a 64/65-byte signature. The redesigned vault's listings are PARTIAL_RESTRICTED with the vault as zone, ONE consideration item and an empty signature, so Overcall's validator would refuse them and Overcall's book never lists them. That is the design (owner decision D1 = A(ii); L-04 dropped, D2 = b).
overcallOrderShape.listingsApi: https://overcall.finance/api/orders — not called by anything in this repository any more. Do not add a call.

46630.name: Robinhood Chain Testnet
46630._VERDICT: NOT a useful rehearsal target for Stonkhouse. Overcall's own Valorem Clear DOES exist on 46630 at 0x0059Df7C6229373a5AFC0685B0EE8777f59BAcbc (an earlier pass recorded it as absent; the R7-R8 adversarial re-check found it, byte-identical to mainnet), but it is unusable for us: the Overcall cycles set on it are hand-set by their operator and lapsed, there is no official NVDA Stock Token (the StockFactory has deployed TSLA, AMZN, PLTR, NFLX, AMD only), no Chainlink RHNVDA feed, and Overcall's mocks (NVDA, USDG, feed) are not the tokens the vault is built for. The redesigned vault does not need a registry, so the registry rows below are moot. The code-size limit is the same 98,304 B as mainnet. A mainnet fork with `--code-size-limit 98304` is the only place to compress a week into minutes; the vault may there be rehearsed against Overcall's Clear or our own (DeployClear.s.sol, rehearsal step A0).
46630._whatItIsGoodFor: A free smoke test of the deploy script, constructor wiring, role grants, Sourcify verification against a live chain, the real Robinhood Stock token transfer/approve/uiMultiplier path and Ponder's live-chain sync, against TSLA instead of NVDA with a stand-in price feed. Skip the Valorem/Seaport legs, or bring our own Clear.
